Probe noop.sh, rep_drv.sh
measured.declared_unassigned_assoc_reads_as_loade: `declare -gA R` (no assignment) makes `${R[@]@a}` expand to 'A' on both bashes; `declare -gA R=()` / `R=()` / unsetting the last element give ''. kuse.sh therefore declares `__KK_UNITS=()` — the first version declared it unassigned and the §7.4 guard then read 'kbool loaded' after a plain `source kuse.sh` (kkore 004 caught it; 009 now pins it). Probe g.sh
measured.P8_detectable_without_extdebug: `source FILE` WITHOUT arguments pushes FILE on BASH_ARGV with BASH_ARGC 1 (evalfile.c). WITH arguments the top entry is never that: bash pushes the arguments (a TOP-LEVEL `source F ARG` pushes them and leaves them stale on BASH_ARGV afterwards — critic C12) or nothing. So kk.unit tests BASH_ARGC[0]==1 && BASH_ARGV[0]==BASH_SOURCE[1] (under extdebug it skips its own frame: ARGC index 1, ARGV offset ARGC[0]). Detection holds on 5.2.37 and 5.3.9 for plain, with args, in a function, set -- in a function, no-slash, via PATH, extdebug. Known false negative: a single argument equal to the unit's own path, or a STALE top entry equal to it (`source wrap.sh FILE` where wrap.sh does `source "$1" x`). An inherited caller "$@" does not count as arguments
measured.KBOOL_HOME_colon_question_exits: the P1 user-unit line 1 `${KBOOL_HOME:?kbool not loaded}` with neither kbool nor KBOOL_HOME EXITS a non-interactive shell (rc 127 seen from the parent; nothing after the source runs) — it does not just fail the source. Probe uu.sh
measured.FUNCNAME_frame_test: a function defined in a unit and called at the depth of the unit's first load has BASH_SOURCE == the unit file at the same bottom-relative index; only FUNCNAME[k]=='source' tells a source frame apart, so the C12 on-stack test checks both (009 pins it with unit fnu)
measured.kk_uses_already_loaded: R9: `kk.uses NAME` of a loaded unit 115/110 us (5.2/5.3, round 1) -> 27-30 / 25-27 us; `kk.uses A B` 143/127 -> 47-54 / 43-48 us. Cause measured: bash copies a function's whole body on EVERY call (execute_function -> copy_command); the 150-line one-piece kk.uses cost ~70 us per call just to copy. Fix: kk.uses = a ~25-line wrapper (fast path: per argument one DONE test + one HIT compare, keyed by the absolute calling file) + kk._uses (the body). The same effect makes kk.unit's skip path 44-49 us (a split there is possible but was not asked). Probe worker_u1a/hot.sh, hot2.sh, hot3.sh

deviations: P5/U13' index shape: the index is lazy at TWO levels — the first name lookup builds only the candidate map (stem -> files <stem>.sh in search order, one glob per path entry, no file read); a candidate's header is read when its stem is looked up, result cached per name (a miss as ''). Same answers as a full index of headered files with first-match-wins, but the first lookup is 4-6 ms instead of 15-25 ms (gate <= 10 ms). Reason: the full header read cannot meet the gate on this machine (measured)

U34 'not done' for PLAIN sources: bash gives no way to see a plain source's rc, so a plain-sourced unit counts as complete once its source frame has returned (lazily marked at the next kk.unit/kk.uses), unless a loader error happened while it was loading (a failing kk.uses called from its file scope, or a header error/cycle of a unit it sources) — that taints the innermost loading unit and a later kk.uses of it says 'not completely loaded' (rc 2) until kk.unit --forget. A plain-sourced unit failing by its own `return N` with no loader error stays undetectable (documented in kuse.sh). The literal reading (registered + not done by kk.uses = error) would make P7 / every 'test sources unit X, unit Y does kk.uses X' fail

loader messages: `kbool: error: ...` / `kbool: WARNING: ...` on stderr, printed unless VERBOSE_KKLASS=quiet (the kk.warn rule), not kk.debug: a loader error is a compile error, not a member's rc-1 miss
KK_UNIT_DIR is a plain global shell variable (not exported to the environment): it is meaningful only while a unit is being sourced in THIS shell; 'exports' in U17 read as 'provides'

kk.unit and kk.uses refuse to work (rc 2) unless kbool.sh is loaded (the [kbool] sentinel): this keeps the loader guard exact — the registry is non-empty iff kbool.sh is loaded — even when kuse.sh is sourced on its own (kklass 128, tcustomapplication do that)

kbool.sh registers the system units kuse, klib, kerr, kvar, kcfg AND itself as unit `kbool` (the sentinel, so `kk.uses kbool` is a no-op); on any failure it empties the whole registry and restores KBOOL_HOME (unset or the preset value), so the guard stays off and a retry works; KBOOL_HOME is always set to the folder kbool.sh was sourced from (a preset KBOOL_HOME pointing elsewhere is overwritten on success — config precedence is U1b)
KBOOL_HOME = the lexically normalised root only when `<normalised>/kbool.sh -ef BASH_SOURCE`, else the absolute spelled root (a symlinked `..` keeps the physical spelling)

kk.unit --forget: rc 0 forgotten, 1 not registered, 2 no name / `kbool` / the unit is loading right now; it calls kk._unit_forget_class CLASS (if defined — kklass, U2) for every class filed by kk._unit_add_class, then drops all registry entries. kk.uses' forget-on-failure uses the same drop. Added kk._unit_current (RESULT = the unit being loaded) as the hook U2 needs to file a class under its unit
kbool.sh executed (bash kbool.sh) prints an error and exits 2

REPLACED (R3, owner 2026-10-06 'найти и сравнить'): kk.uses NAME always resolves the name (caller dir -> project -> system) and compares it with the registered unit: same file (string first, -ef on mismatch) -> skip; another file -> rc 2 "unit 'a' is already loaded from X; here it resolves to Y". A loaded name that NO lookup finds (the system units until their U3 headers, kbool) counts as the registered file. Resolutions are cached per (caller dir, name) in __KK_UNIT_RES; the fast path per (absolute caller file, name) in __KK_UNIT_HIT (value = the registered file it matched, so a re-registration from another file misses it)

REPLACED (R4): header detection skips blank and `#` lines (shebang, a comment block) inside the one 512-character read; `kk.unit <stem>` must be the first or second remaining line; a line cut by the 512 limit does not count; CR ignored. Rule written into §7.4

R1 (accepted-in-part deviation 2, narrowed): the U34 taint is set only on STRUCTURAL errors inside a unit's load — a header error (usage, U33), a cycle, a unit-name/identity clash, a use of an incomplete unit — never on a dependency that is not found, has a bad name, or fails with its own rc (the unit may handle it: `kk.uses opt || fallback`)

R2: kuse.sh has no re-source guard variable any more (an inherited __KLIB_USE_SOURCED skipped the table declarations in a child); every source redefines the functions and kk._unit_tables repairs each table (an assigned assoc is kept; unset / unassigned / scalar / indexed is replaced by an empty assoc — attribute read with `${!t@a}` under a function-local `set +u`). kk._unit_reset = unset + kk._unit_tables. kbool.sh checks one function per system unit after sourcing it (klib kk.isInt, kerr ke.setTrap, kvar kv.framePush, kcfg kc.alias) -> rc 2. Ownership marker: first __KK_BOOT_PID (= $), REPLACED in R14 by the one-element assoc __KK_LOADED ([on]=1) — see review_round_2
R8: kk.uses in a shell whose registry is not its own (`${__KK_LOADED[@]@a} != A`) sources $KBOOL_HOME/kbool.sh first when KBOOL_HOME is set and the file exists; else rc 2
R7: kk.unit --forget refuses (rc 2) every unit kbool.sh registered — kbool, kuse, klib, kerr, kvar, kcfg (__KK_UNIT_SYS); an unknown name is still rc 1

R10: executed-detection is exact — a function called from kbool.sh's top level sees FUNCNAME[1]=='source' when sourced (also `bash -c 'source "$0"' kbool.sh`), 'main' when executed; kk._kbool_boot is unset on the failure path too (the rc is carried in __kk_unit_rc, no file-scope `set --`)

R12: a source of ANOTHER copy of kbool.sh (not -ef the registered one) while kbool is loaded is a no-op with one `kbool: WARNING: X is ignored: kbool is already loaded from Y` line (silenced by VERBOSE_KKLASS=quiet); the same file in any spelling stays silent
R11: kk._unit_index_build runs with a function-local, unset GLOBIGNORE
R5 (owner): the user-unit line 1 is `source "${KBOOL_HOME-}/kbool.sh" || return 2` (fixture + §7.4); with neither kbool nor KBOOL_HOME the source fails with rc 2 and the caller continues
found_in_U1a: for U3/U4 (C11 consequence, not new): a unit loaded by kk.uses runs INSIDE kk.uses, so file-scope `local` and `declare` without -g become kk.uses locals and vanish; checked: no kcl unit / kklass / kkore file has one today (only kcl/*/bench.sh, which are not units)
for U3/U4 (critic C11): add a lint test that fails on file-scope `declare`/`local`/`typeset` without -g in every unit file (they would become kk._uses locals)

for U1b (critic C13): KBOOL_HOME has two meanings — U5 makes it the strongest config source, while kbool.sh overwrites a preset value with its own folder on success (accepted deviation 6); U1b must decide which wins

for U3 (measured in R9): bash copies a function body per call, so kk.unit's no-op skip path (44-49 us of the 188-193 us re-source) could drop further with the same wrapper split as kk.uses — frame indices in a split kk.unit shift by one
